gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured failure rate by length: in Linus Tech Tips' bench test of 53 HDMI 2.1 cables, 9 failed, and only half of the 15 ft cables passed. Monoprice's failures came only on its 10 ft and 15 ft cables, from signal integrity, while 6 ft Amazon Basics cables passed at 48 Gbps.
standout_why: I compared this against the cited iTechGuides guide, the cited Cable Matters extension page, and Shinforce's uncited 'best HDMI extension cables for gaming rooms' page. I tried twice to open the cited Bestways UGREEN HD151 page, but it returned HTTP 429 both times. iTechGuides gives the 'may work at 4K/60 but fail at 4K/120' warning with no measurement behind it. Its only length figure is ViewSonic's report that standard cables passed compliance testing up to 10 m. The Cable Matters page makes no test or certification claim. Shinforce (Devon Kastelic) reports only pass/fail results on consoles, with no measured figures. None of them puts a measured number on how a 48 Gbps link holds up as length grows.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's warning about total length with a number, and it favours the short passive UGREEN HD151 for 4K120 when the existing cable plus the extension stays at about 6–10 ft. Once the total passes 10 ft, the measured failures argue for an active extension (Cable Matters) or one certified run of the full length instead. It does not rank UGREEN against Cable Matters directly, because nobody has published a measurement of either extension.

findings.label: HDMI 2.1 cables that failed Linus Tech Tips' bench test
findings.source_title: I Spent a THOUSAND Dollars on HDMI Cables.. for Science (Linus Tech Tips, transcript)
findings.note: Video published 2021-11-08. 53 cables from 17 makers, about $1,000 in total, run through a cable tester that shows an eye diagram (the lab isn't named in the transcript). 2 failed on continuity only; 7 failed signal integrity at HDMI 2.1 speeds, some with continuity faults too. Read from a third-party transcript site, not LTT's own page. 9/53 = 17%.

findings.label: 15 ft HDMI 2.1 cables that passed Linus Tech Tips' test
findings.source_title: I Spent a THOUSAND Dollars on HDMI Cables.. for Science (Linus Tech Tips, transcript)
findings.note: Transcript: 'only 50% of our 15t cables passed' (caption typo for 15 ft). The presenter concludes that 'if you're going anywhere over 10 ft with HDMI 2.1 you're asking for trouble.' This is the figure that applies to an existing cable plus an extension.

findings.label: Monoprice cables that passed Linus Tech Tips' test
findings.value: 11 of 15; all 4 failures were 10 ft or 15 ft cables, from signal integrity
findings.source_title: I Spent a THOUSAND Dollars on HDMI Cables.. for Science (Linus Tech Tips, transcript)
findings.note: These were passive Monoprice HDMI 2.1 cables tested in 2021. The test did not include the Monoprice 8K Certified Active cable ChatGPT showed.

findings.label: Short (6 ft) cable result in Linus Tech Tips' test
findings.value: Amazon Basics 6 ft cables passed HDMI 2.0 and HDMI 2.1 (48 Gbps) testing
findings.source_title: I Spent a THOUSAND Dollars on HDMI Cables.. for Science (Linus Tech Tips, transcript)
findings.note: Shows that short budget cables can pass at 48 Gbps. No cable in the test failed DC resistance; the video says that matters more for passive runs of 25 ft and longer.

findings.product: Cable Matters 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable (male to female)
findings.label: Certification and power, from the maker's page
findings.value: No Ultra High Speed certification listed; active; optional Micro-B USB power, 'recommended, especially for longer distances or 8K signals'; one direction only (female end to source)
findings.note: These are maker specs, not measurements. The page shows a 6.6 ft size option and says it can 'Extend an 8K cable run by 5 meters (16.4 feet)'. The price field was blank. The page makes no test or eye-diagram claims.

findings.label: Ultra High Speed certification requirement
findings.value: Every certified Ultra High Speed model must pass testing at an HDMI Forum Authorized Testing Center, including EMI testing; HDMI LA also buys cables at retail and has them retested
findings.source_title: Ultra High Speed HDMI Cable - Bandwidth Up To 48Gbps (HDMI.org)
findings.note: The page does not mention male-to-female extension cables or couplers. It gives the shopper a lab-tested standard to check an extension against.
